steps.say: Trains run to a timetable. In this lesson you signal one train through Hollins Cross. Press Next.

Train 2H05 has appeared at the left edge of your area. It is in the TRAINS list on the right, with where it calls next: Hollins Cross (HXC) platform 2, and its booked time. It will wait at H1. Press Next.

Click the SIMPLIFIER tab above the train list. The simplifier is your timetable: every train booked through your box, where it calls, which platform (Plat) and its booked arrival (Arr) and departure (Dep).
2H05 is booked into platform 2, arriving 08:04 and leaving 08:05. Click TRAINS to go back to the train list whenever you like. Press Next.
Set the route from H1 to H3, so the train can move up to H3.
Now route it into its booked platform: H3 to H7, platform 2. A train sent to the wrong platform costs penalty points in a real game.

Watch the train. As it leaves each track circuit, the white route behind it turns grey: this is sectional release, which frees track for other routes as soon as the train has passed. The step ends when 2H05 stands at platform 2.

2H05 is at platform 2. It leaves when its time comes, but only if its signal is clear. Set the route out: H7 to H9. It is booked to leave at 08:05, so it may wait a little; 2× or 4× beside the clock speeds time up.
Last, set H9 to the edge of your area: click H9, then the small square at the right-hand end of the line. The train then leaves your area.

Well done. A train that runs behind its booked time is late: the train list and the simplifier show how late (OT on time, 3L three minutes late). In a real game late trains cost penalty points; tutorials keep no score. Next lesson: junctions, auto-working and handing trains to the next box. Press Next to finish.
